author: _Gill
body:
To whom it may concern,

Hello, my name is Max Gillette, and I have been with the Avicus Network (or servers affiliated with it) for longer than I can remember. I am making not only an appeal, but also an apology. For those reading this that do not know of my infraction, I will explain. I was intoxicated greatly, and I logged onto teamspeak. I leaked a document from about a year ago that contained criticism on past Jr Mods. I leaked this not to cause chaos, but to attempt to help a former mod with the mistakes that some people saw in her. Technically, I didn't even leak the information (look to Mariam Webster's Dictionary for the term "leak"). I believe that I deserved punishment for my immature actions, but I do not think it should have been permanent. Before I make my argument, I would like to apologize to the staff members affected by my releasing of information. I am sorry to whom it affected negatively (which is no one), but I do apologize for my immature behavior.

To begin with my case, I would like to point out the fact that I was attempting to do this for the good of another. I never intended for that document to be publicly released (and it wasn't). I gave it to the person for them to learn from their mistakes, and to help them in total. I would also like to argue that since this information wasn't sensitive, I should be granted a lighter sentence for my actions. If these were the Senior Mod Interview questions, then the case would be different. 

My next point I would like to bring up was that I never intended for the document to be leaked. I already spoke about this above, but I would like to elaborate. Mariam-Webster's dictionary states that a leak (in terms of information) is to "To give (secret information) to someone so that it becomes known to the public." I never intended for the information to be made public, and I knew that it wouldn't. I easily trusted the person I gave it to to not use this information maliciously. As I predicted, the person didn't, but actually did the polar opposite thing and turned me in for it (kinda a dick move if you ask me). I do agree that I should have been punished, but I do not think it should be permanently. And I believe that it has been over two weeks, and therefore a suitable punishment (but this is up to the Sr Staff).

My next point is that even though I was quite rudely banned off of the server publicly, shamefully, and embarrassingly; I didn't decide to leak the actual sensitive information that I still hold. When I was banned, a staff member quickly came into the public channel I was in, basically said thanks, your banned (not even asking or talking to me like I was a person), and swiftly banning me from the TS. Honestly, I think this was immature, and quite frankly stupid. This person talk to me calmly, didn't explain the reasoning, and didn't actually tell me to not do it again. In the state I was in, I was filled with anger, sadness, and a sense of betrayal. My friend had turned on me, I was banned off of the server that I have played on for longer than anyone else here, and all of this was done publicly. Honestly speaking, I cried for a while. I was drunk, and I literally could have done anything. But, I decided to be the bigger person, and wait out my problem, and this is where it has led me.

There are more points that I could probably bring up, and I most definitely will if this is denied. I would prefer to not talk over forums with an Admin or Sr Mod who can deal with this. If there are any problems, please call me on my Skype so we can discuss this. 

In conclusion, I think I have served the rightful sentence for the action that I did (although that is up to you). I believe that I should be unbanned on Teamspeak for these simple reasons.

Thank you for reading and please be swift to respond,
Max Gillette

title: My Appeal: TeamSpeak

replies.author: Newcleus
replies.body:
Gill,
Let me establish my points, and then I will give you the verdict.

Firstly;
"To give (secret information) to someone so that it becomes known to the public."
Technically speaking, people who were not Senior Staff that were intended to have the link are regarded to as the "public" in the definition you stated.

Secondly, I've never been intoxicated before, but I don't understand why you would try to help someone with their mistakes while under such an influence. Even if you were to help them, you probably would not have even been punished if you did something such as screenshotting the responses on their column as opposed to sending them the entire document that you copied.

Lastly, you did not intend  to use it for helping someone with their mistakes, I was told by multiple people in the chat that you were bragging about how you had their verdicts and reasoning out loud, and that was part of what fueled me to ban you. Don't try to say it was for constructive purposes when you were A.) Drunk and B.) Using it to show off some of the things you have.

So here's the verdict.
I am shortening your ban to 1 more week, and you will be unbanned after that. However, you must remove all documents from your libraries and never even speak of those sorts of documents again, or I will not hesitate to punish you again. Also, I recommend you don't come on TS or other Avicus services while under the influence of alcohol or other substances, as it may result in you doing similar actions and receiving harsher punishments.

If you want to discuss anything about this, you can message me on Skype, which you have my contact.
Regards,
Straightened,
Avicus Network Administrator
